page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-60 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the Tau T2D machine family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 60 dedicated physical cores with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration, providing 60 vCPUs. It is equipped with 240 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the t2d-standard-60 demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, placing in the top 10% on stress-ng multi-core tests. It also shows strong capabilities in multi-threaded tasks, including bzip3 decompression, software compilation with Clang, and Passmark database operations, all ranking in the top 25%. Cached read-only memory bandwidth is strong, though uncached large-block read and write operations fall into the average tier.

Tradeoffs include a lack of bundled local storage and weak performance in large-scale LLM text generation, where text generation for a 70B model falls into the bottom 25%. However, its dedicated core execution model and high multi-core throughput make it highly efficient for multi-threaded workloads. The instance is suited for database operations, software compilation, web serving, and medium-scale prompt processing tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-60 is an x86_64 general-purpose instance within the Tau T2D family, featuring 60 dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 physical cores and 240 GB of RAM. Lacking local storage and GPUs, it relies on external network storage. The instance delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 10% on stress-ng multi-core benchmarks, alongside strong multi-threaded decompression and database execution. However, uncached memory bandwidth remains average, and text generation for large 70B language models is weak. Given its dedicated core allocation and high resource density, the t2d-standard-60 offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy, multi-threaded workloads. It is best suited for database operations, software compilation, and medium-scale prompt processing.
